texts.value: Hydrolyzes linear guanidino acids to form urea and the corresponding amines. Displays specificity for substrates having a negatively charged head group and short chains including taurocyamine, guanidino propanoic and butanoic acids. May protect cells by detoxifying potentially harmful amounts of guanidino acids. Metabolizes L-arginine with low efficiency
Nitrogen metabolism; urea cycle; L-ornithine and urea from L-arginine: step 1/1

Highly expressed in liver and kidney. Also found in skeletal muscle, fetal liver, brain, testis, skin and the gastrointestinal tract. Within brain, expression is higher in the cerebral cortex with lower levels in the medulla and spinal cord
Belongs to the ureohydrolase superfamily. Arginase family
Initially proposed to function as agmatinase but this activity was not proved when using the purified enzyme. A recent study showed that it rather functions as a guanidino acid hydrolase

features.description: increased guanidino hydrolase activity toward taurocyamine; can hydrolyze guanidinopropanoate with low efficiency; inactive toward L-arginine; dbSNP:rs6429757
